S No  Registrar's order with  Signatures  22.03.2023 C482 No. 657 of 2022  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Mohit Kumar, learned counsel alongwith Ms. Meenu, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. T.C. Agarwal, learned Deputy A.G. assisted by Ms. Lata Negi, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Krishan Kumar Verma, learned counsel for the private respondent no. 2.

The applicant though not named in the FIR No. 173 of 2020, which was registed at P.S. Kunda,
District Udham Singh Nagar, it has been alleged by the complainant-Sunil Kumar therein that Mr.
Sukhvir was indulged in a malice transaction for the exchange of an immovable property, which has been referred to therein.
The matter was investigated upon and it was that during the course of investigation, a final report was submitted, the Investigating Officer in the Charge-Sheet No. 804 of 2021 dated 28.08.2021, has observed that in fact, the role of the present applicant was to the effect of extending the financial assistance to the named accused persons therein and it was on the basis of the said extension of financial assistance to the Sukhbir Singh, the present applicant has been roped up in the commission of offence as per the observations made by the Investigating Officer in the Charge-Sheet.
The present applicants were consequently summoned in Criminal Case No. 622 of 2022, "State of Uttarakhand vs. Sukhvir and others", by an order of 21.03.2022.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The counsel for the applicant submits that if the statements, which has been placed on record,
particularly, the statement of Sushil Kumar is taken into consideration, he submits that as per the observations made in Para-2, Sub-clause (5), his only role was that he was instrumental in helping of Sukhbir Singh in entering into a transaction for the sale of property, which was subject matter of the FIR and there was a connivance between Sukhbir Singh and the present applicant.

In reference thereto, the statement of Sunil Kumar, as recorded under Section 161 becomes relevant,
which has been filed alongwith counter affidavit, wherein as per Clause 2, the name of the present applicant does figured to be involved in the commission of offence.

This Court is of the view that since, up to what extent, the present applicant was instrumental in commission of an offence in connivance with Sukhbir Singh, as it has been complained of with the FIR, for the offences under Section 420 and 120-B of IPC, that can only be best decided after appreciation of evidence to be made by the Trial Court.

The platform of Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not available for the purposes of scrutinization of evidence to test the veracity of the involvement of the accused person, who has been found to be involved in commission of offence during the course of investigation, because that in itself entails a detailed scrutiny of evidence and the statements, to be recorded during the course of trial, before coming to any plausible conclusion.

Since, offences for which the present applicant has been summoned in Criminal Case No. 622 of 2022, "State of Uttarakhand Vs. Sukhvir Singh", are for the offences under Section 420 and 120-B of IPC, the learned counsel for the applicant submits that his C-482 Application may be decided in terms of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another as reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51, and, he may be granted liberty to surrender before the Court, within a period of two weeks' from today and seek his bail in accordance with the guidelines framed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the said judgment in relation to the offences which carry a sentence of less than seven years.
Subject to the aforesaid liberty left open for the applicant, to surrender within a period of two weeks'
from today, the C-482 Application is not being ventured into on merits by this Court.
The C-482 Application is, accordingly, dismissed.
